development_end_to_end.purpose: One-core end-to-end ratios: 1.4.1, 1.5.0 slow and 1.5.0 fast, public inputs.
development_end_to_end.interpretation: The experimental 1.5.0-fast variant includes FMA engine trigamma; arrays-only retains Boost engine trigamma and is the final fast-mode choice. Slow and 1.4.1 are controls. These are development measurements, superseded for paper ratios by the frozen measured-commit run.
development_end_to_end.service_event: The development-library installer restarted slurmd during this allocation; job remained active/exclusive with no restart or policy change. No command exceeded contention limits.

boost_log1p_check.choice: Keep glibc for engine scalar log1p. Boost 1.74 log1p(double, double policy) delegates to glibc on this platform with domain checks; measured slower or tied over all five ranges. Earlier own division-based AVX2 remains the fast array choice.

slow_mode_dev2_continuity.comparison_note: Checkpoint elapsed-time headers and cache manifests with temporary paths/mtimes are excluded; all scientific table bytes agree.

agreement_scope: Untimed final-source checks: eight bulk tables match the separately checked Cook-fixed baseline in each division mode; five edgeR reference datasets preserve all discovery identities and filters. Diagnostic elapsed times are not kernel or workload timings.

cross_path_bit_identity.scope: The fixed-operation-order kernels reproduce their mode-specific known-answer digests on native AVX2/FMA, forced-portable x86-64 and AArch64 under QEMU. Slow lgamma and negative-argument fast lgamma use platform libm and are outside this kernel identity claim.
